items.label: What you say when you’re not speaking

blocks.heading: What he talks about.

lines.text: You can be surrounded by colleagues and still on your own.
You’re doing the job well and struggling quietly underneath it.
You carry everyone else’s feelings and nobody asks about yours.
There’s a conversation you keep moving to next week.
Small unsaid tensions add up until everyone is tired.
Left unsaid long enough, this becomes what the organization calls a *performance problem*.

image.alt: An audience listening closely in a darkened conference room

blocks.text: In the room, Stephen says these things out loud, so people recognize them in their own team. Then he gives leaders a practical, research-informed way to work with them: clear the silent friction, strengthen trust, and rebuild it quickly after a breakdown.

items.label: Short
items.text: Dr. Stephen de Wit draws on more than twenty years as a therapist and researcher to help leaders turn human tension into trust, and trust into performance.

items.label: Medium
items.text: Dr. Stephen de Wit has spent more than twenty years as a therapist, researcher, speaker and facilitator, from transformational retreats to research with homeless veterans and people living with dementia. He now helps leaders read the human dynamics in their teams and turn them into practical ways to strengthen trust and performance under pressure.

items.label: Long
items.text: For more than twenty years, Dr. Stephen de Wit has worked as a therapist, researcher, speaker and facilitator, in rooms where trust was fragile and the silence was loud. His work has ranged from transformational retreats to research with homeless veterans and people living with dementia. What he saw there is the basis of his talks: when people don’t feel seen, safe or heard, performance erodes. Today he helps leaders clear silent friction, rebuild trust after a breakdown and build the kind of trust that helps people stay. He is a Research Associate at Ontario Tech University and has delivered 170 keynotes.

intro.heading: Stage introduction
intro.note: For your host to read when welcoming Stephen to the stage.
paragraphs: For more than twenty years, Dr. Stephen de Wit has worked as a therapist, researcher, speaker and facilitator. He has sat with people when trust was fragile and the silence was loud.
What he saw there is the basis of his work: when people don’t feel seen, safe or understood, performance erodes.
Today he helps leaders clear invisible friction, rebuild trust and shape cultures where people lean in.
Please welcome Dr. Stephen de Wit.

av.heading: AV at a glance
items: A wireless headset microphone, as Stephen moves through the room. A wireless lavalier works if needed.
A professional sound system suited to the room, with fresh batteries.
Projection and screens the whole audience can see, with HDMI if Stephen uses his laptop.
At least one confidence monitor at the foot of the stage, and a countdown timer he can see.
A soundcheck of at least 30 minutes in the room on the day, before doors open.
